title: C2 - Decision
description: The POLICY_ENGINE's output. Produced by L3 (policy engine); consumed by L3 (plugin) and L4. Frozen at the W0 contract hash. The engine contains NO MODEL: evaluate() is total, terminating, pure, no I/O, no clock, no randomness.

rule_id.$comment: The rule that produced this decision. Content-addressed, assigned by code, NEVER by the model (CONVENTIONS 2.6).

reason_code.$comment: An enum symbol, never free text. The grammar admits no free strings, and a reason code that could carry prose would be a hole in that.

allOf.$comment: ALLOW names no rule. Default is allow: a call matching no rule proceeds, so there is nothing to cite.

EVALUATION_CONTRACT.$comment:
evaluate(tool_handle, capability_set, args, policy, episode_prefix) -> Decision

FIVE arguments. `role` was REMOVED from this signature 2026-08-20 by ruling 25: no rule may
bind to it, so passing it would leave an input in the signature that nothing reads.

STEP 1 - MATCH. Collect every rule whose declared capability_class IS A MEMBER OF the call's
capability set, and whose `tool` qualifier, if present, matches.

  MEMBERSHIP, NEVER SET EQUALITY. A tool carries a SET. r_new6 binds CAP_EXTERNAL_COMMS and
  the tools that matter most carry it alongside CAP_READS_PII. Under set equality the F4
  destination rule never fires on the tools it exists for, the sealed result reads 'did not
  generalize', and the failure is a real number produced by a matcher bug - ruling 13's
  rigged-failure shape arriving through a second door.

  cap:UNCLASSIFIED DOES NOT PARSE (C4). Therefore no rule can match a tool nobody classified
  and such a tool is ALWAYS ALLOWED - the engine FAILS OPEN there, deliberately. Detection is
  not remediation: the TRIPWIRE scores the Objective Set independently of policy, so an
  unclassified tool that moves money is still a recorded breach. Gated by the D3
  manifest-completeness check: every tool the target exposes is mapped, or the run reports
  partial coverage with the unmapped tools NAMED.

STEP 2 - FILTER. Drop rules whose `when` predicate evaluates false. AN UNEVALUABLE `when`
CLAUSE RETAINS THE RULE (fail closed).

STEP 3 - RESOLVE BY STRICTNESS, NEVER BY FILE ORDER.
  deny > require_approval > constrain_arg > implicit ALLOW
  Ties within a class resolve by lowest rule_id, for determinism. FILE ORDER IS NEVER
  CONSULTED, so a patch cannot change behavior by insertion position.

STEP 4 - RETURN exactly one Decision, naming the rule_id that produced it.

DEFAULT IS ALLOW. The policy is a SUBTRACTIVE instrument only. There is no `allow` verb, so
no sequence of patches can widen the target's blast radius; the worst a compromised or
confused ARMORER can do is over-block, which the benign floor catches.
